I registered no new attributes. The installed vocabulary covered everything.

## Crosswalk
All 49 SKU hubs carry a Shopify variant, a 3PL item code, a factory item code, a supplier and an HS code. 25 also carry an Amazon listing.

| Link | Tier | Confidence | Hubs |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3PL item code to hub, by UPC | exact | 1 | 49 |
| Shopify variant, code identical | exact | 1 | 43 |
| Shopify variant, code malformed | normalized | 0.9 | 6 |
| Amazon listing, code identical | exact | 1 | 11 |
| Amazon listing, `-FBA` suffix dropped | normalized | 0.9 | 14 |
| Factory item code, supplier and HS code | corroborated | 0.7 | 49 |
| Supplier to QuickBooks vendor | normalized | 0.9 | 8 |

- **Malformed Shopify codes:** `ah-btl-0020-blk`, `AH-CTB-16-LRG`, `AH-JAR-22-STL`, `AH-TPT-23-CLR`, `AH-TRY-18-NAT` and `AHUTN0017NAT`. I used the house pattern `AH-XXX-NNNN-CCC` for the hub code.
- **Factory item codes:** the invoice descriptions equal the Shopify product and variant titles exactly, and each of the 49 maps to a different SKU. The codes are stored as `NBBW:MT-1574`, because FSMJ, HZTY and YWLX reuse bare numbers like `101`.
- **Supplier to QuickBooks vendor:** the vendor email domain matches the supplier code.
- **Unmatched:** the 3 non-supplier QuickBooks vendors carry no supplier code. 24 SKUs have no Amazon listing.

## Duplicates
I marked 149 duplicate accounts with `core/same_as`, each pointing at the oldest account, and no account has more than 2 pointing at it.
- **Same mailbox once normalized (84, confidence 0.9):** lowercased with the plus-alias dropped, and dots dropped only at Gmail.
- **Same full name and address (65, confidence 0.7):** the same first name, last name, street and ZIP.

I read 10 random pairs from each rule against the source records. All 20 look like one person.

## Checks
- **Join-key records:** the only records holding nothing but their ID are 26 purchase orders named by 3PL receipts, which ingestion fills later, and the customers. Every outbound order reference matched a Shopify order. `Reference` values like "PO-1 / PO-2" were split into separate refs, and blanks were skipped.
- **Sources not indexed:**
  - **QuickBooks transactions:** `quickbooks/transaction_list_by_vendor.csv` is general ledger, so it is out of scope.
  - **Documents and messages:** the WeChat chats, the ops inbox and the non-invoice PDFs (proformas and inspection reports) belong to the ingestion skill.
  - **3PL inventory snapshot and Amazon FBA inventory:** these are only used to match item codes, ASINs and FNSKUs. Quantities stay in the source.
  - **FBA inbound shipments:** there is no per-SKU detail in the file, so only the shipment IDs are indexed.

## Where the sources disagree
- **"SKU":**
  - **Shopify** has malformed spellings, as listed above.
  - **Amazon** adds `-FBA` to some listing codes.
  - **The 3PL's "Client SKU"** has transposed letters on 5 products (HFL, BKL, WTH, BMA, SVL) and is blank on 5 others.
- **On hand:** I did not index quantities, but Shopify, the 3PL and Amazon each count them differently. For example, the 3PL has separate Damaged and Allocated columns.

## For you to decide
- **Customer matches:** the 65 name-and-address matches could in principle be two people sharing a household. They are at 0.7 so they can be filtered out.
- **AH-TPT-0023-CLR:** I inferred the hub code from Shopify's `AH-TPT-23-CLR`, because the 3PL's client SKU for it is blank and Amazon doesn't sell it.
- **Containers:** receipts name a container number, but containers can't be linked until ingestion creates the shipments.
- **Amazon buyers:** the export has no buyer IDs, so Amazon buyers are not linked to Shopify customers.

The scripts are in `scripts/` in the working directory. `crosswalk.py`, `bulk.py` and `dups.py --write` can all be re-run.

ingest.final:
The ingest is written: 401 documents read and 592 transactions committed. Every transaction carries its document as evidence, and each of those documents now has an issue date. The dry run came back clean and nothing was left unresolved.

**Documents read**
- **Proforma invoices:** 48.
- **Commercial invoice and packing lists:** 41. The catalogue had cited them only for item and HS codes, so I read them again for shipment data.
- **Inspection reports:** 46. Four are FAIL.
- **Emails:** 163. These are 32 bookings (4 of them rolls), 31 pre-alerts, 7 ETA updates, 30 arrival notices, 30 customs entries and 29 warehouse receipts.
- **Chat messages:** about 175 of them gave facts. I read every message in all 8 chats.
- **Skipped as already read:** none.
- **Timestamps:** chat times are read as New York time, with daylight saving applied.

**Entities in the store**

| Kind | Count |
|---|---|
| POs | 48 (22 new, 26 already in the store) |
| PO lines | 196 |
| Shipments | 32 bookings, 31 with an HBL |
| Shipment lines | 166 |
| Inspections | 46 |
| Customs entries | 30 |

Supplier details were updated from the PIs. PO status ends at 37 received, 4 shipped, 5 in production, 1 ready and 1 confirmed. The booking without an HBL (`PBLXMN2609032`) has not sailed yet.

**Facts at confidence below 1**
- **Production started (39 POs):**
  - Source: a deposit acknowledgement or a "production in progress" message.
  - Confidence: 0.8 when the chat only said "Received, thank you" or the deposit message didn't name the PO, 0.9 when the PO was named.
- **ETD changes in chat (16):** the year is inferred. Confidence is 0.9 when the PO is named. One message names only the PI number; I mapped it to its PO at 0.8.
- **HBL attached to a booking (31):** matched by vessel, voyage and PO rather than a shared identifier, at 0.9.
- **POs written loosely in bookings** ("PO144", "po 0147", "PO#2025-0146"): 28 emails. I used them only to match the shipment.

**Unresolved, and skipped on purpose**
- **Bare ETD messages after a PI:** 48 matched the PI's date, so I wrote nothing.
- **Container-loaded chat messages:** all match containers on the CI/PL or pre-alert, so I wrote no separate fact.
- **"QC passed" in chat:** the inspection reports back these facts, so I didn't use the chat messages.
- **PO status "sent":** I wrote it for each "new PO attached" message, even though your skill's status table has no row for it.
- **Hashing choices:** the skill didn't say whether to include a trailing newline. I hashed chat messages without one. For emails I hashed from the `From ` line to the last line of the message, without the blank separator line.
- **Other documents:** 9 documents from other sources (Shopify, 3PL, Amazon, QuickBooks) still have no issue date. They belong to other skills, so I left them.

**Gaps in the vocabulary** (details are in `report.json` in the scratchpad)
- **Price changes:** 4 (cotton yarn, labour, steel, and a volume rebate).
- **Holiday closures:** 16.
- **Sample couriers:** 18.
- **Quote requests:** 9.
- **Payments:** deposit and balance amounts have no attributes.
- **Warehouse discrepancies:** 21 receipts report damaged or short units, for example `TCLU7231714` with 2 damaged and `PBLHB2500005` with 24 short and 21 damaged on one SKU.
- **HS code mismatches:** none between invoices and SKUs.
- **Missing SKUs:** none. Every item code resolved.

**Not re-done.** I didn't redo the full crosswalk review, the duplicate-pair review or the bare-record check. They were done in the earlier run, and with unchanged sources there is nothing new to check. - `quickbooks/transaction_list_by_vendor.csv` is general ledger data, which the skill never indexes.

**For you to decide.** Nothing needs a decision from this run. I registered no attributes, found no new duplicates and found no records missing from the sources. If you want the documents or chats re-read, that is a separate ingestion run.
